business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real Estate Property Management and Rental Screening Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law, Samoan custom, and codified statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa–China Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (signed 2008, entered into force 2010)
PACER-Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, entered into force 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2018 (Act No. 18 of 2018); International Companies Act 1987 (Act No. 13 of 1987), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015; International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2016; Companies Act 2001 (Act No. 5 of 2001)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies of all proposed directors and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of each holder's country (e.g., People's Republic of China Ministry of Public Security for Chinese UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Samoa is not a Contracting State to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified bank reference letter / banker's confirmation of good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank (signature authenticated by notary public in the bank's jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or lease agreement) for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or landlord, notarized before a notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and KYC questionnaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed ultimate beneficial owner, executed before a notary public or equivalent authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic PEP list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the Samoa domestic sanctions list. Screening must be completed and documented prior to filing for incorporation, with results retained for a minimum of six years as required by the AML/CFT Act 2018.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property (ROCIP) - Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Online Name Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered corporate names must be in English using Latin/Roman script. Samoan-language names are permissible. Names in Chinese characters or any non-Latin script are not accepted as the legal name; a romanized transliteration of a Chinese trading name may be recorded as an alias, but all statutory documents and the Memorandum of Association must be in English. An International Company must end with 'International Company', 'IC', 'Ltd', 'Limited', or a corresponding prescribed suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice, stating the grounds of objection and a proposed amended name. The Registrar must issue a decision within 14 working days. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Companies Act 2001; such application must be lodged within 21 days of the Registrar's final decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible. An International Company must maintain a physical registered office address in Samoa located at the licensed registered agent's place of business; the address must be a real, occupied premises capable of receiving service of process, and virtual-only offices are not accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% quantified probability within the first 12 months of operation, based on Samoa's risk-based AML/CFT supervision framework for non-licensed, low-risk PropTech SaaS entities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government name clearance and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Registrar of Companies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule under the Companies Regulations 2001

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registry declaration and AML/CFT filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the AML/CFT Act 2018 and International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2016

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC / UBO piercing compliance verification (directors and ultimate beneficial owners)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark plus recognized consular fee schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts, in particular sections 6 (Incorporation), 7 (Certificate of Incorporation), 10 (Registered Office) and 11 (Registered Agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation and Memorandum and Articles of Association (Form 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under Samoa's International Company regime. The authorized capital is stated in the Articles of Association; no escrow or capital deposit rule applies. At least one share must be issued on incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the International Company having appended their signatures to the Articles of Association, the name of the Company is confirmed and the Registrar of International Companies is directed to file the Application for Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office in Samoa shall be the premises of [Registered Agent], which is also appointed as registered agent, and that the directors named in the consent forms are appointed as first directors. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the authorized share capital is allotted and issued to the subscribers as set forth in the share subscription schedule, and that [Secretary/Finance Officer] is empowered to maintain statutory registers and arrange payment of incorporation fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Registry of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance request for the proposed company name. Obtain written name approval from the Registry and execute a registered agent agreement with a licensed Samoa registered agent. Confirm the physical registered office address in Apia and secure the landlord or servicing agent's written consent for use as the registered office.
required_dossiers: Name clearance request form
Proposed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent consent form
Registered office consent from the office premises provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or prohibited character, submit up to three alternate proposed names for accelerated re-screening without paying a fresh name fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Registry of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the International Companies Act 1987. Have each subscriber execute the Articles, have the first directors execute consent-to-act forms, and arrange notarization and legalization of signatures through the registered agent. Verify that the registered agent's certification is attached before lodgement.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Application for Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed)
Consent to act as first director
Subscriber register / share subscription schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query on execution formalities, cure the defect by filing a notarized statement of correction or re-executed signature pages together with the original query notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Payment of Incorporation Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registry counter and online lodgement portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the completed Form 1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles and all supporting consents. Pay the official filing fee via direct bank transfer to the Samoa International Finance Authority account, using the SIFA file reference as remittance detail. Obtain a stamped acknowledgment of lodgement from the Registry.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form 1
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (duplicate wet-ink copy)
Bank remittance receipt for the official filing fee
Registered agent covering letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is not matched due to remittance reference error, produce the bank receipt to the SIFA Treasury section and request re-allocation to the correct application file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Opening of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review of the filed documents, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and incorporation date. The company secretary then opens the statutory registers, including the register of members, register of directors, and register of charges, and physically maintains them at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Statutory register of members
Statutory register of directors and officers
Share certificate templates for issued shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a typographical or administrative error, file a request for administrative correction supported by the original certificate and the company's constitutional documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Setup and Annual Compliance Direction
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Licensing and Compliance Desk and the Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate is issued, the registered agent lodges the official agent acceptance with SIFA, issues executed share certificates to the subscribers, and files the confirmation of the registered office. The company secretary prepares a governance calendar for branch filing of annual fees, tax-exempt status confirmation, and continued maintenance of the statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Registered agent acceptance notice
Issued share certificates
Letter of consent from the registered office provider
Annual maintenance and licensing fee schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If agent-acceptance records are absent from SIFA's system, file a statutory declaration signed by the directors confirming the agency appointment and request reinstatement of the compliance record.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board engaged; the business is a non-manufacturing remote software service under ISIC 6201 and does not operate a physical production facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no manufacturing or physical industrial operating permit required for cloud-based Property Technology SaaS services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, Samoa – Planning and Urban Management Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA permit under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 because the activity involves no land clearance, physical discharge, or changes to land use. A Category Exemption Notice may be issued if formally requested.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the digital service activity. The company must nonetheless procure cloud hosting services from providers maintaining acceptable wastewater, volatile organic compound, and e-waste take-back standards for data center operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No on-site civil defense clearance is required for the virtual registered office. The registered office landlord's building occupancy certificate and central fire escape certification must be kept on file. If a leased operational office is opened in Samoa, Fire and Emergency Services Samoa inspection certification, structural load approval, and Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour workplace health and safety registration would be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa; official portal www.revenue.gov.ws; Customs Division within MfR administers import/export controls; Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) is the corporate registry for International Companies
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the International Company (IC) with SIFA under the International Companies Act 1987 through a licensed registered agent/trustee in Apia; SIFA issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Step 2: File the TIN application with MfR on the official registration form, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office consent, director/shareholder particulars, and a declaration of offshore business scope (ISIC 6201 SaaS); the Commissioner of Revenue assigns the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). Step 3: Apply to MfR for a Certificate of Tax Exemption confirming the statutory exemption under ICA 1987 s.232 from income tax, VAGST, stamp duty, and all other national taxes; this certificate is provided to banks and counterparties. Step 4: No statutory business license is required for offshore SaaS activity; the IC must maintain its registered agent and file annual returns with SIFA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or US-style entity classification election exists under Samoan law. An International Company receives an automatic, non-revocable statutory tax exemption under ICA 1987 s.232 (as amended), conditional on carrying on business exclusively outside Samoa and deriving no Samoan-source income. No hybrid mismatch, CFC, or equivalent elections are available. Voluntary VAGST registration is not required because the IC is statutorily exempt from VAGST; the Certificate of Exemption is the operative evidence of tax status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 aggregate taxable turnover in any 12-month period triggers compulsory registration under the VAGST Act 2003; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold. An International Company is exempt from VAGST regardless of turnover and is not required to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate operates in Samoa. VAGST-registered persons must file returns electronically via the MfR online portal by the 28th day following the taxable period. Invoices (paper or electronic) must contain the supplier TIN, recipient name, date, description, consideration, and VAGST amount, with a 5-year record-retention requirement. International Companies are outside the VAGST net and issue non-VAGST commercial invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAGST Act 2003, exports of goods and services supplied for the direct benefit of a non-resident outside Samoa are zero-rated. For PropTech/real-estate SaaS (ISIC 6201), the criteria are: (a) the customer is a non-resident not using the software in Samoa; (b) fees are received in convertible foreign currency; (c) the contract and invoice identify the place of supply as offshore. The International Company holds an absolute statutory exemption from VAGST under ICA 1987 s.232, making zero-rating a secondary safe-harbour rather than a primary obligation; refund claims are available only to registered persons and are not necessary for exempt ICs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Export Entry/SAD) or deemed-export statutory declaration for non-tangible digital services
Executed SaaS subscription agreement or commercial invoice naming the non-resident counterparty and stating the offshore place of supply
Bill of lading or airway bill where incidental physical media/hardware is exported
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT payment evidence from the non-resident payer
Certificate of Exemption under International Companies Act 1987 s.232
Digital delivery logs or usage reports evidencing customer utilisation outside Samoa for audit substantiation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: MfR may audit under the Tax Administration Act 2022 with a general assessment window of 5 years, extended to 10 years where fraud or gross negligence is established. Fraudulent zero-rating or export refund claims attract a shortfall penalty of 100% of the tax avoided plus compounding monthly interest at 2%, criminal fines up to WST 100,000 or the tax amount, and imprisonment of directors/officers on conviction. An International Company that breaches the ring-fencing condition by carrying on business with Samoan residents or deriving Samoan-source income automatically forfeits the s.232 exemption, exposing the entity to retrospective re-assessment of income tax (27%), VAGST (15%), and stamp duty with penalty interest; SIFA may also strike off the IC and sanction the licensed registered agent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is not freely convertible outside Samoa. The Exchange Control Act 1976 establishes exchange control administered by the Central Bank of Samoa, and all commercial banks act as authorized dealers. Current account transactions are generally processed on presentation of underlying invoices and supporting documents. Capital account transfers, equity injections, cross-border loans, and dividend or profit remittances require exchange control approval and, where applicable, tax clearance certificates. International Companies are treated as non-resident persons for most exchange control purposes and may maintain foreign currency accounts, but any conversion into WST or transfer to Samoa resident persons must be routed through an authorized dealer and recorded by CBS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must repatriate export proceeds into Samoa through an authorized dealer within the statutory period, normally 90 days from the date of shipment. Unless a specific exemption is granted by the Central Bank of Samoa, 100% of the export receipt must be offered for conversion into WST or deposited into an approved foreign currency account on terms stipulated by the authorized dealer. International Companies conducting exempt offshore business may apply for a standing exemption to retain export earnings in foreign currency, but the exporter must still file exchange control declarations and provide a banker's receipt evidencing inward remittance and conversion for any onshore or export transaction requiring WST settlement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Medium. Offshore digital EMI and payment offerings such as Wise, Stripe, or a third-country electronic money institution cannot serve as the primary settlement account for Samoan treasury purposes because they are not licensed banks under the Central Bank of Samoa Act and cannot operate domestic WST clearing rails. A foreign EMI or payment facilitator may provide collection and disbursement services offshore, but all FX conversion, exchange control reporting, and Samoan standpoint payments must be routed through a CBS-licensed authorized dealer. Where the EMI is used for front-end SaaS subscription and landlord collection, the local bank remains the account of record for regulatory capital, escrow segregation, and FX approval. The arrangement must also be assessed under the Samoa Money Laundering Prevention Act, with the EMI treated as a third-party payment processor rather than a domestic financial institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and at least one ultimate beneficial owner are generally required to appear physically at the account-holding bank's branch in Apia for a mandatory KYC interview before an International Company bank account is activated. Remote video interviews and notarized identity documents are accepted only as supplementary KYC and generally cannot eliminate the in-person requirement for non-resident directors. Some banks permit a one-time remote onboarding waiver for high-credentialed international clients, subject to enhanced due diligence and approval by the bank's compliance committee. In all cases, the registered agent must provide corporate certification, and documents executed outside Samoa must bear notarization and apostille or be legalized by the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company with tax-exempt status and no visible economic substance in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation; International Company register extract; registered agent confirmation from a licensed Samoa International Company service provider; beneficial ownership declaration; board resolution opening the account and appointing authorized signatories; corporate structure and ownership chart; audited or management financial statements; notarized identity and proof of address for all directors and shareholders; reference letters from existing bankers or attorneys; confirmation of no negative regulatory history from the Samoa Financial Services Authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection sourced from high-volume real estate sales, DLT tokens, or a private trust with opaque funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign exchange control application form submitted to the Central Bank of Samoa; source of funds breakdown with sale and purchase agreements, escrow release statements, trust deed, or token listing/prospectus; bank statements demonstrating unencumbered funds in the remitter's account; board resolutions approving the capital injection; register of charges or loan agreement if the inflow is shareholder debt; tax clearance certificate or confirmation of tax status from the Samoa Inland Revenue Service; accounting records showing the funds to be posted to share capital or shareholder loan accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected pass-through volume for PropTech rent collection, landlord disbursements, and SaaS subscriptions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow agreement or agency/service contract detailing the flow of funds between tenants, landlords, and platform operators; detailed intercompany or treasury policy on receipt conversion and disbursement timing; complete schedule of counterparties and proof that landlords and tenants are outside prohibited lists; sanctions screening evidence on each onboarding entity; AML/CFT procedural manual covering transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting; audit trail software and integration with SWIFT payment messages; declaration that funds held on behalf of third parties are segregated from the International Company's proprietary funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loan funds must be routed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the remitter's licensed bank directly to the International Company's account at a CBS-authorized dealer. The payment reason or purpose code on the wire must clearly state 'equity injection', 'capital contribution', or 'shareholder loan - credit to capital account' as applicable; the beneficiary reference should contain the Samoa International Company registration number (IC-####-WS) and the unique board resolution reference. The local bank will hold the receipt in a capital escrow folder pending completion of source of funds verification, exchange control approval, and KYC release. For amounts above CBS threshold levels, the corporate customer must submit the CBS exchange control application form, a board resolution approving the capital injection, and evidence of the shareholder's capacity to fund. The bank will issue a foreign exchange purchase confirmation or inward credit advice, and the funds will be recorded in the books as issued share capital or director/subordinated shareholder loan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier, landlord, and SaaS settlement payments are cleared through the domestic authorized dealer using SWIFT MT103 for individual wire payments, with MT202 used only for interbank/treasury transfers. For documentary trade settlements, a commercial letter of credit (LC) is the required rail, with the presenting beneficiary supplying invoice, packing list, ocean/airway bill, insurance certificate, and certificate of origin as applicable. USD-denominated disbursements to third-party payment processors such as Stripe may be made through U.S. correspondent bank clearing (ACH direct, Fedwire, or SWIFT to Stripe's settlement bank) only after the local bank has performed sanctioned jurisdiction screening and issued a foreign exchange approval reference or conversion instruction. All outbound diaspora disbursements originating from the PropTech platform should be batch-prepared and transmitted with payment memo fields carrying the landlord ID, property reference, and tenant lease contract reference to satisfy CBS recordkeeping and AML transaction monitoring obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts (WST/USD) traded with a CBS-licensed authorized dealer for documented trade, rent, or financing flows with a maximum tenor of 12 months

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD executed offshore in a permissible jurisdiction, provided the underlying exposure is substantiated and CBS exchange control approval is obtained for the hedging arrangement
Cross-currency basis swaps between USD and WST for long-term real estate SaaS receivables or property funding structures
Foreign currency option contracts purchased from an authorized dealer or approved international bank on an end-user basis to hedge rollover FX exposure; speculative uncovered positions are prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days of the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 50–500 (approximately USD 20–180); persistent non-filing after a notice period of 3 months triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution under the International Companies Act 2012.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Government Renewal Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 40% of the renewal fee for late payment; continued non-payment for six months from the due date authorizes the Registrar of International Companies to strike the entity off the register and dissolve it without further notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Registered Agent Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (filed with SIFA on the company's behalf)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation, or within 14 days of any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure by the registered agent to maintain or confirm beneficial ownership records results in the agent's suspension or revocation of license by SIFA and may lead to the company's deregistration for non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a standard Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 2012. Mandatory independent audit applies only to licensed banks, insurance undertakings, and licensed trustee or custody businesses. A non-regulated PropTech SaaS platform qualifies for the blanket audit exemption if it does not conduct financial services for the public.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the Samoa Institute of Accountants for entities that voluntarily prepare audited financial statements; offshore tax-exempt International Companies are not required to file financial statements with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent must maintain a Register of Beneficial Owners and confirm its accuracy annually on or before the anniversary of incorporation. Any shareholding transfer during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members, and changes to beneficial ownership must be notified to the registered agent within 14 days of the triggering transaction.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book and Corporate Seal Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,500 per year for licensed registered agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable — audit exempt; voluntary IFRS audit by a Samoa-licensed firm typically USD 3,500–6,000 if required by overseas stakeholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Samoa International Company total tax exemption under s.198 International Companies Act 1987; Samoa domestic standard corporate rate 27%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and withholding taxes on dividends, interest, and royalties; no minimum capital tax; the only periodic government charge is the SIFA annual license fee (approx. USD 250-500) payable to the Samoa International Finance Authority

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SIFA Annual Return (IC Annual Confirmation under the International Companies Act 1987), filed electronically through the licensed Samoa registered agent on the SIFA portal; no income tax return (IRD Form IR-101) is required because the IC is tax-exempt; Economic Substance Return (Form ESR-1) must be separately lodged with SIFA when a relevant activity exists
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due within 28 days after the anniversary of incorporation; SIFA annual license fee payable by the anniversary date (SIFA renewal cycle generally aligned with 31 December for pre-existing companies)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and IC registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter name exactly as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa (physical street address, not P.O. Box)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the registered agent's physical Samoan office address

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Licensed registered agent name and license number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The appointed Samoan-licensed agent must co-sign the return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors details (full names, nationality, residential addresses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Minimum one director; any nationality permitted; corporate directors allowed
List all UBOs for the SIFA Beneficial Ownership Register; nominee arrangements must be disclosed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of no domestic business activity in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm no transactions with Samoan residents and no Samoan real estate holdings
If 'yes', file Form ESR-1 with SIFA and attach CIGA narrative; false negative declaration is a criminal offence

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty WST 50 plus WST 25 per month of default (International Companies Act 1987); failure to pay the annual SIFA license fee triggers strike-off from the register, restoration surcharges, and disqualification of directors in Samoa

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - dividends paid by a Samoa IC to non-resident shareholders are fully exempt from Samoan withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa ICs generally cannot obtain a Certificate of Tax Residency because they are exempt from Samoan tax; to invoke any DTA relief (Samoa's limited DTA network, e.g., Norway), file a Treaty Relief Application with the Ministry of Revenue, submit the IC certificate, audited substance evidence, and TRC request; without a TRC the foreign payer applies its domestic WHT at source; the IC's practical route is the domestic zero-rate exemption rather than treaty relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid by a Samoa IC: 0% domestic WHT (exempt); a Samoan domestic company paying royalties or interest to a non-resident is subject to 10% statutory WHT; existing DTA rates (where a Samoa DTA applies) may reduce this to 5% for royalties and interest subject to TRC issuance

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory threshold and no Local File/Master File mandate under Samoa law; however, the Economic Substance (International Companies) Regulations 2019 impose ESR-1 mandatory substance reporting for all relevant-activity ICs regardless of revenue level; TP documentation (intercompany agreements, pricing methodology, benchmark analysis) should be maintained for all intercompany SaaS royalty and service transactions to survive foreign CFC and substance audits
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance (International Companies) Regulations 2019 apply: an IC deriving income from relevant activities (including IP holding, financing, distribution, or provision of services such as the PropTech SaaS platform) must file Form ESR-1 with SIFA annually, maintain adequate qualified staff and physical premises in Samoa, incur sufficient local operating expenditure, and demonstrate that core income-generating activities are managed and conducted in Samoa; failure attracts monetary penalties, strike-off, and exchange of information with treaty partners

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exempt IC earns SaaS licensing royalties or intercompany service revenue without any personnel, premises, or management activity in Samoa; fails to file ESR-1 or falsely declares no relevant activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty up to WST 10,000 for first offence and WST 20,000 for subsequent offences; compulsory disclosure of beneficial ownership to foreign tax authorities; strike-off and retroactive loss of the s.198 tax exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face imprisonment up to 5 years; foreign CFC and anti-avoidance rules may attribute the PropTech platform income directly to the founders in their home jurisdiction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: IC trades with Samoan residents, holds Samoan real estate, or provides property-management services within Samoa, violating s.8 International Companies Act 1987
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 25,000; deregistration; the s.198 exemption is voided retroactively for the offending period and the IC becomes taxable at the 27% domestic rate on all Samoan-source income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax (27%), penalties, and interest; repeat offenders face disqualification from acting as directors in Samoa

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify, record, or update ultimate beneficial ownership in the SIFA register; moving client funds or investor capital through unregistered payment channels in breach of the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fine up to WST 100,000; freezing of bank accounts; termination of Stripe Billing and ACH Direct payment rail access by U.S.-regulated processors; mandatory AML de-risking
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Wilful breach carries imprisonment up to 14 years, asset forfeiture orders, and travel bans against directors, compliance officers, and the beneficial owner

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Facilitating offshore tax evasion / cross-border fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa IC as a secrecy shell to conceal beneficial ownership of U.S., New Zealand, or Australian real-estate SaaS revenue without substance, or exploiting the Low-Risk Standard AML tier to process suspect investor deposits derived from rental-screening fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Information exchange via AEOI/CRS and TIEAs; cancellation of correspondent banking relationships; adverse risk rating by FATF members; civil confiscation of platform revenues in foreign courts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and UBOs face civil restitution, extradition, asset freezes, and imprisonment in the jurisdiction prosecuting the tax evasion or fraud; Samoa authorities may suspend the IC and surrender records under mutual legal assistance
